newsitem.title: USA: Dlr slumps to US close after FOMC holds U.S. rates.
newsitem.headline: Dlr slumps to US close after FOMC holds U.S. rates.

text.p: The dollar slumped against major currencies Tuesday after Federal Reserve policy makers surprised many in the financial markets by holding interest rates steady, prompting fresh concerns about rising inflation, dealers said.

Currency investors who had banked on a rate hike sold dollars on news that the central bank's monetary policy arm, the Federal Open Market Committee, voted against raising short-term rates. A narrow majority of analysts had predicted a modest increase at the conclusion of Tuesday's FOMC meeting.
After an initial bounce from support at 1.5050 marks and 109.50 yen, the dollar slumped again as stop-loss selling and nervous long liquidation took their toll.
Many economists at the Fed and in the private sector have warned that the central bank must soon raise interest rates to ease rising inflation pressures in a vigorous U.S. economy.

Since higher interest rates tend to strengthen a nation's currency, investors who had expected higher rates fled into the Japanese yen and European units immediately after the FOMC announced its decision, dealers said.

"The market needed to feel like 25 basis points (added to the current fed funds rate at 5.25 percent) was in and the Fed would do it in front of the election. Now the dollar looks a little bit soft," said Mark Gargano, managing director for foreign exchange at First Union National Bank.
The dollar touched the 1.50-marks level late Tuesday and dealers expected the losses to end either at or just below that key technical level for now.
Current support sits at 1.4980/50 marks and 108.80/50 yen, dealers said.
